source.text: וַנֵּ֜פֶן וַנִּסַּ֤ע הַמִּדְבָּ֨רָה֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יַם־ס֔וּף כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וַנָּ֥סָב אֶת־הַר־שֵׂעִ֖יר יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And we turned and set out [toward] the wilderness [by the] way of [the] Sea of Reeds, as spoke Yahweh to me; and we went around the hill country of Seir many days.

en.L: And we turned and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to me; and we went around the hill country of Seir many days.
en.B: So we turned back and headed into the wilderness by the Red Sea road, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me, and we spent a long time going around the hill country of Seir.
en.R: Then we turned around and went back into the desert on the road toward the Red Sea, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me. For a long time we kept going around the hill country of Seir.

es.L: Y nos volvimos y partimos hacia el desierto por el camino del mar de los Juncos, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me había dicho; y rodeamos la región montañosa de Seír muchos días.
es.B: Entonces dimos la vuelta y nos dirigimos al desierto por el camino del mar Rojo, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me había dicho, y durante mucho tiempo anduvimos rodeando las montañas de Seír.
es.R: Después dimos media vuelta y regresamos al desierto por el camino que va hacia el mar Rojo, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me había dicho. Durante mucho tiempo estuvimos dando vueltas por las colinas de Seír.

fr.L: Et nous nous sommes tournés et nous sommes partis vers le désert, par le chemin de la mer des Joncs, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me l’avait dit ; et nous avons contourné la montagne de Séir pendant de nombreux jours.
fr.B: Nous avons donc fait demi-tour et pris la direction du désert par la route de la mer Rouge, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me l’avait dit, et nous avons longtemps tourné autour de la montagne de Séir.
fr.R: Alors nous avons fait demi-tour et nous sommes repartis dans le désert, sur la route de la mer Rouge, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me l’avait dit. Pendant longtemps, nous avons tourné autour des collines de Séir.

sw.L: Kisha tukageuka, tukasafiri kuelekea nyikani kwa njia ya Bahari ya Matete, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameniambia; tukaizunguka nchi ya milima ya Seiri siku nyingi.
sw.B: Basi tukarudi nyuma, tukaelekea nyikani kwa njia ya Bahari ya Shamu, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoniambia, na kwa muda mrefu tukaizunguka nchi ya milima ya Seiri.
sw.R: Kisha tuligeuka, tukarudi jangwani kwa njia iendayo Bahari ya Shamu, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameniambia. Kwa muda mrefu tulizunguka-zunguka katika vilima vya Seiri.

ko.L: 그리고 우리는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하신 대로 방향을 돌려 갈대 바다 길로 광야를 향해 떠났고, 여러 날 동안 세일 산지를 돌아다녔다.
ko.B: 그래서 우리는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하신 대로 돌아서서 홍해로 가는 길을 따라 광야로 떠났다. 그리고 오랫동안 세일 산지를 돌아다녔다.
ko.R: 그래서 우리는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하신 대로 돌아서서, 홍해 쪽으로 가는 길을 따라 광야로 되돌아갔습니다. 우리는 오랫동안 세일 산지 둘레를 돌아다녔습니다.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had spoken to me: Israel now obeys the order of 1:40
decisions.reason: After the people refused to enter the land and were beaten at Hormah, God told them to turn and go back into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds (1:40). This verse uses the same words to say that this time they did as they were told.

decisions.choice: the way of the Sea of Reeds: the road south toward the gulf east of Sinai
decisions.reason: "Sea of Reeds" is the name of the sea of the crossing (Exodus 13:18; 15:4), and it is also used for the gulf at Elath and Ezion-geber (1 Kings 9:26; verse 8). Here it names the road leading south toward that gulf, as in Numbers 21:4.

decisions.choice: we went around the hill country of Seir many days: a long time spent moving about the region of Edom
decisions.reason: Seir is the mountain country of Edom, south-east of the Dead Sea (Genesis 36:8). "Many days" covers the long years in the wilderness; verse 14 counts thirty-eight years from Kadesh-barnea to the Zered. The verb pictures circling round, not a straight march.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:4: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

decisions.choice: the passé composé at every level ("nous nous sommes tournés", "nous avons fait demi-tour"), with imparfait and plus-que-parfait
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: As set for Deuteronomy at 1:1: the whole chapter is Moses speaking to the people and retelling their journey, and a story told in speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew introduces the quotation with "saying", which English does not need after "said".

records.literal_gloss: Enough for you going around the hill country this; turn yourselves northward.

en.L: '[It is] enough for you, going around this hill country; turn northward.
en.B: 'Your circling of this hill country has gone on long enough. Turn north now.
en.R: 'That is enough going around these hills. Now head north.

es.L: “Bastante [es] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} rodear esta región montañosa; {{plural_you:vuélvanse|volveos}} hacia el norte.
es.B: “Ya {{plural_you:han|habéis}} dado bastantes vueltas alrededor de estas montañas. {{plural_you:Diríjanse|Dirigíos}} ahora hacia el norte.
es.R: “Ya basta de dar vueltas por estas colinas. Ahora {{plural_you:vayan|id}} hacia el norte.

fr.L: “[C’est] assez pour vous de contourner cette montagne ; tournez-vous vers le nord.
fr.B: “Vous avez tourné assez longtemps autour de cette montagne. Dirigez-vous maintenant vers le nord.
fr.R: “Cela suffit de tourner autour de ces collines. Maintenant, partez vers le nord.

sw.L: 'Imewatosha kuizunguka nchi hii ya milima; geukeni mwelekee kaskazini.
sw.B: 'Mmeizunguka nchi hii ya milima kwa muda wa kutosha. Sasa geukeni mwelekee kaskazini.
sw.R: 'Inatosha kuzunguka vilima hivi. Sasa nendeni upande wa kaskazini.

ko.L: '너희가 이 산지를 돌아다닌 것으로 충분하다. 북쪽으로 방향을 돌려라.
ko.B: '너희가 이 산지를 돌아다닌 지 충분히 오래되었다. 이제 북쪽으로 가거라.
ko.R: '이 산지를 돌아다니는 것은 이제 그만하면 되었다. 이제 북쪽으로 가거라.

decisions.choice: enough for you: it is time to stop and move on
decisions.reason: The same words opened God's command at Horeb, "You have stayed long enough at this mountain" (1:6). Each time they mark the end of one stage of the journey and the start of the next.

decisions.choice: northward: toward the lands east of the Dead Sea and the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel had been in the region south of Edom. Turning north takes them up past Edom and Moab toward the country of Sihon (verse 24) and the Jordan.

source.text: וְאֶת־הָעָם֮ צַ֣ו לֵאמֹר֒ אַתֶּ֣ם עֹֽבְרִ֗ים בִּגְבוּל֙ אֲחֵיכֶ֣ם בְּנֵי־עֵשָׂ֔ו הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּשֵׂעִ֑יר וְיִֽירְא֣וּ מִכֶּ֔ם וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And the people command, saying, You [are] passing in [the] territory of your brothers, [the] sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir; and they will be afraid of you, and you will take heed very much.

en.L: And command the people, saying, "You [are] about to pass through the territory of your brothers the sons of Esau, who live in Seir; and they will be afraid of you, and you must take great care.
en.B: And tell the people: "You are going to cross the land of your relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will fear you, and you must take great care.
en.R: Give the people this command: "You are going to travel through the land that belongs to your relatives, the descendants of Esau. They live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.

es.L: Y manda al pueblo, diciendo: ‘{{plural_you:Ustedes están|Vosotros estáis}} a punto de pasar por el territorio de {{plural_you:sus hermanos|vuestros hermanos}}, los hijos de Esaú, que habitan en Seír; y ellos {{plural_you:les|os}} tendrán miedo, y {{plural_you:ustedes tendrán|vosotros tendréis}} mucho cuidado.
es.B: Y da esta orden al pueblo: ‘{{plural_you:Ustedes van|Vosotros vais}} a cruzar el territorio de {{plural_you:sus parientes|vuestros parientes}}, los descendientes de Esaú, que viven en Seír. Ellos {{plural_you:les|os}} tendrán miedo, pero {{plural_you:ustedes deberán|vosotros deberéis}} tener mucho cuidado.
es.R: Dale al pueblo esta orden: ‘{{plural_you:Van|Vais}} a pasar por la tierra de {{plural_you:sus parientes|vuestros parientes}}, los descendientes de Esaú. Ellos viven en Seír. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} tendrán miedo, así que {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} mucho cuidado.

fr.L: Et commande au peuple, en disant : ‘Vous [êtes] sur le point de passer par le territoire de vos frères, les fils d’Ésaü, qui habitent en Séir ; et ils auront peur de vous, et vous prendrez bien garde.
fr.B: Donne au peuple cet ordre : ‘Vous allez traverser le territoire de vos proches parents, les descendants d’Ésaü, qui habitent en Séir. Ils auront peur de vous, et vous devrez être très prudents.
fr.R: Donne cet ordre au peuple : ‘Vous allez passer par le pays de vos proches, les descendants d’Ésaü. Ils habitent en Séir. Ils auront peur de vous, alors faites bien attention.

sw.L: Nawe uwaamuru watu, ukisema, "Ninyi [mko] karibu kupita katika mpaka wa ndugu zenu, wana wa Esau, wakaao Seiri; nao watawaogopa, nanyi mtajihadhari sana.
sw.B: Uwape watu agizo hili: "Mtapita katika nchi ya ndugu zenu, wazao wa Esau, wanaoishi Seiri. Watawaogopa, nanyi mjihadhari sana.
sw.R: Uwaamuru watu hivi: "Mtapita katika nchi ya ndugu zenu, wazao wa Esau. Wao wanaishi Seiri. Watawaogopa, kwa hiyo kuweni waangalifu sana.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 백성에게 명령하여 말하여라. "너희는 세일에 사는 너희 형제 에서의 자손의 영토를 지나가려 한다. 그들이 너희를 두려워할 것이니, 너희는 매우 조심하라.
ko.B: 그리고 백성에게 이렇게 명령하여라. "너희는 이제 세일에 사는 너희 친족, 에서의 자손의 땅을 지나가게 된다. 그들이 너희를 두려워할 것이니, 너희는 아주 조심하라.
ko.R: 백성에게 이렇게 명령하여라. "너희는 너희 친척인 에서의 자손이 사는 땅을 지나가게 될 것이다. 그들은 세일에 산다. 그들이 너희를 두려워할 것이니, 아주 조심하여라.

decisions.choice: your brothers the sons of Esau: the Edomites, a people related to Israel
decisions.reason: Esau was the twin brother of Jacob, who is Israel (Genesis 25:24-26), and his descendants lived in Seir (Genesis 36:8-9). Israel and Edom are "brothers" as nations (Numbers 20:14; Deuteronomy 23:8), and that kinship is part of the reason Israel must not fight them.

decisions.choice: they will be afraid of you, and you must take great care: Edom's fear is no excuse for Israel to take advantage
decisions.reason: The two clauses belong together: because Edom will be afraid, Israel must be all the more careful not to start a fight. Verse 5 says what that care means.

decisions.choice: the message to the people runs from here to the end of verse 7
decisions.reason: God gives Moses words to pass on to the people. Verses 5-7 carry on the same message: what Israel must and must not do in Edom, and why.

decisions.choice: pass through the territory: compare Numbers 20:14-21
decisions.reason: In Numbers 20 the king of Edom refused to let Israel cross his land, and Israel went around it (Numbers 21:4). Here the emphasis is on how Israel was to behave as it went by Edom's people, buying what it needed (verse 6). The route probably ran along Edom's edge rather than through its heartland.

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "brothers", meaning a related people. Balanced and Readable say "relatives" so that the reader does not think of Esau's own brothers; Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: "vos proches parents" (B), "vos proches" (R); "vos frères" (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relatives", as the English does. Plain "vos parents" would first be heard as "your mother and father", so French adds "proches".

decisions.choice: "친족" (Balanced) and "친척" (Readable) for "brothers" meaning the related people of Edom; Literal keeps "형제"
decisions.reason: The Edomites are kin, not fellow Israelites, so the "동족" used for Israelites in 1:16 would be wrong; Balanced and Readable say "relatives" as the English does.

source.text: אַל־תִּתְגָּר֣וּ בָ֔ם כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֤ן לָכֶם֙ מֵֽאַרְצָ֔ם עַ֖ד מִדְרַ֣ךְ כַּף־רָ֑גֶל כִּֽי־יְרֻשָּׁ֣ה לְעֵשָׂ֔ו נָתַ֖תִּי אֶת־הַ֥ר שֵׂעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not engage in strife with them, for not I will give to you of their land even [the] treading of [the] sole of a foot, for [as] a possession to Esau I have given the hill country of Seir.

en.L: Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even the treading of the sole of a foot, for I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau [as] a possession.
en.B: Do not start a fight with them, because I will not give you any of their land, not even room enough to set your foot on. I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau as his possession.
en.R: Do not try to fight them. I will not give you any of their land, not even a footprint's worth. I have given the hills of Seir to Esau's family to be their own.

es.L: No {{plural_you:los provoquen|los provoquéis}}, porque no {{plural_you:les|os}} daré de su tierra ni siquiera lo que pisa la planta de un pie, porque a Esaú le he dado la región montañosa de Seír [como] posesión.
es.B: No {{plural_you:entablen|entabléis}} pelea con ellos, porque no {{plural_you:les|os}} daré nada de su tierra, ni siquiera el espacio para poner un pie. A Esaú le he dado la región montañosa de Seír como posesión suya.
es.R: No {{plural_you:intenten|intentéis}} pelear con ellos. No {{plural_you:les|os}} voy a dar ni un pedazo de su tierra, ni siquiera lo que ocupa una pisada. Las colinas de Seír se las he dado a la familia de Esaú para que sean suyas.

fr.L: Ne les provoquez pas, car je ne vous donnerai rien de leur pays, pas même la place où se pose la plante d’un pied, car c’est à Ésaü que j’ai donné la montagne de Séir [en] possession.
fr.B: N’engagez pas le combat avec eux, car je ne vous donnerai rien de leur pays, pas même de quoi y poser le pied. J’ai donné la montagne de Séir à Ésaü pour qu’elle soit à lui.
fr.R: N’essayez pas de leur faire la guerre. Je ne vous donnerai pas un morceau de leur pays, pas même la place d’un pas. J’ai donné les collines de Séir à la famille d’Ésaü : elles sont à eux.

sw.L: Msiwachokoze, kwa maana sitawapa chochote cha nchi yao, hata mahali pa kukanyaga wayo wa mguu, kwa sababu nimempa Esau nchi ya milima ya Seiri [kuwa] milki.
sw.B: Msianzishe ugomvi nao, kwa sababu sitawapa sehemu yoyote ya nchi yao, hata nafasi ya kuweka mguu. Nimempa Esau nchi ya milima ya Seiri iwe milki yake.
sw.R: Msijaribu kupigana nao. Sitawapa hata kipande cha nchi yao, hata nafasi ya hatua moja. Nimeipa jamaa ya Esau vilima vya Seiri viwe vyao.

ko.L: 너희는 그들과 다투지 말라. 내가 그들의 땅은 발바닥으로 밟을 만큼도 너희에게 주지 않을 것이다. 내가 세일 산지를 에서에게 소유로 주었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그들과 싸움을 일으키지 말라. 나는 그들의 땅을 발 디딜 만큼도 너희에게 주지 않을 것이다. 세일 산지는 내가 에서에게 소유로 주었다.
ko.R: 그들과 싸우려고 하지 말라. 나는 그들의 땅을 발자국 하나만큼도 너희에게 주지 않을 것이다. 세일 산지는 내가 에서의 자손에게 주어 그들의 땅이 되게 했다.

decisions.choice: provoke: stir up a quarrel or a war
decisions.reason: The verb means to stir oneself up against someone, to start hostilities. It is used again for Moab (verse 9) and Ammon (verse 19), and then, turned round, in God's command to fight Sihon (verse 24).

decisions.choice: the treading of the sole of a foot: the smallest piece of ground
decisions.reason: The space a foot covers when it steps is the least amount of land one could own. Israel is to take nothing at all from Edom.

decisions.choice: I have given ... as a possession: God gives lands to other peoples too
decisions.reason: The word "possession" is the one used for Israel's own land. God has given Seir to Esau, Moab to Lot's descendants (verse 9) and Ammon's land to them as well (verse 19). The asides in verses 10-12 and 20-23 add that other peoples, too, received their lands by God's hand.

decisions.choice: Esau's family
decisions.reason: "Esau" stands for his descendants, the people of Edom. Readable says so.

source.text: אֹ֣כֶל תִּשְׁבְּר֧וּ מֵֽאִתָּ֛ם בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֑ם וְגַם־מַ֜יִם תִּכְר֧וּ מֵאִתָּ֛ם בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וּשְׁתִיתֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Food you will buy from them for silver, and you will eat; and also water you will buy from them for silver, and you will drink.

en.L: Food you shall buy from them for silver, and you shall eat; and also water you shall buy from them for silver, and you shall drink.
en.B: You are to buy food from them with money so that you can eat, and you are to pay them money for water to drink as well.
en.R: Pay them money for the food you eat. Pay them for the water you drink too.

es.L: Comida {{plural_you:comprarán|compraréis}} de ellos por plata, y {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}}; y también agua {{plural_you:comprarán|compraréis}} de ellos por plata, y {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Deberán|Deberéis}} comprarles con dinero la comida que {{plural_you:coman|comáis}}, y también {{plural_you:pagarán|pagaréis}} con dinero el agua que {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Páguenles|Pagadles}} la comida que {{plural_you:coman|comáis}}. {{plural_you:Páguenles|Pagadles}} también el agua que {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}}.

fr.L: Vous leur achèterez de la nourriture à prix d’argent, et vous mangerez ; et vous leur achèterez aussi de l’eau à prix d’argent, et vous boirez.
fr.B: Vous leur achèterez avec de l’argent la nourriture dont vous aurez besoin pour manger, et vous leur paierez aussi l’eau que vous boirez.
fr.R: Payez-leur la nourriture que vous mangez. Payez-leur aussi l’eau que vous buvez.

sw.L: Mtanunua chakula kwao kwa fedha, mpate kula; na pia mtanunua maji kwao kwa fedha, mpate kunywa.
sw.B: Mtanunua chakula kwao kwa fedha ili mle, na pia mtawalipa fedha kwa maji ya kunywa.
sw.R: Walipeni pesa kwa chakula mtakachokula. Walipeni pia kwa maji mtakayokunywa.

ko.L: 너희는 음식을 그들에게서 은으로 사서 먹고, 물도 그들에게서 은으로 사서 마셔라.
ko.B: 너희는 그들에게 돈을 주고 음식을 사서 먹고, 마실 물도 돈을 주고 사라.
ko.R: 너희가 먹을 음식은 그들에게 돈을 주고 사라. 마실 물도 돈을 주고 사라.

decisions.choice: you shall buy ... you shall buy: two different verbs with the same sense here
decisions.reason: The first verb is used for buying grain (Genesis 42:2-3); the second means to make a purchase or bargain (Hosea 3:2). The same second verb can also mean "dig", but "from them for silver" shows that buying is meant.

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: There were no coins yet. Payment was made in weighed pieces of silver, so "silver" is the ordinary word for money.

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "money", which is what the silver was used as; Literal keeps "silver".

source.text: כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ בֵּֽרַכְךָ֗ בְּכֹל֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֶ֔ךָ יָדַ֣ע לֶכְתְּךָ֔ אֶת־הַמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה זֶ֣ה׀אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֥א חָסַ֖רְתָּ דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: For Yahweh your God has blessed you in all [the] work of your hand; he has known your walking [through] the wilderness the great this; this forty year[s] Yahweh your God [has been] with you; not you have lacked a thing.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you in all the work of your hand; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has known your walking [through] this great wilderness. These forty years {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [has been] with you; you have not lacked a thing."'
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed all that your hands have done. He has cared for you as you made your way through this great wilderness. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has been with you for these forty years, and you have never gone without anything."'
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed everything you have done. He has taken care of you on your long trip through this huge desert. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has been with you all these forty years, and you have always had what you needed."'

es.L: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha bendecido en toda la obra de tu mano; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha conocido tu andar [por] este gran desierto. Estos cuarenta años {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios [ha estado] contigo; no te ha faltado nada.’”
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios ha bendecido todo lo que han hecho tus manos. Él ha cuidado de ti mientras recorrías este gran desierto. Durante estos cuarenta años {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios ha estado contigo, y nunca te ha faltado nada.’”
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios ha bendecido todo lo que has hecho. Te ha cuidado durante tu largo viaje por este desierto inmenso. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios ha estado contigo todos estos cuarenta años, y siempre has tenido lo que necesitabas.’”

fr.L: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a béni dans tout le travail de ta main ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a connu ta marche [à travers] ce grand désert. Voilà quarante ans que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu [est] avec toi ; tu n’as manqué de rien.’”
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu a béni tout ce que tes mains ont fait. Il a pris soin de toi pendant que tu traversais ce grand désert. Depuis quarante ans, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est avec toi, et tu n’as jamais manqué de rien.’”
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu a béni tout ce que tu as fait. Il a pris soin de toi pendant ton long voyage dans cet immense désert. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu a été avec toi pendant ces quarante ans, et tu as toujours eu ce qu’il te fallait.’”

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekubariki katika kazi yote ya mkono wako; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} amejua kutembea kwako [katika] nyika hii kubwa. Miaka hii arobaini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako [amekuwa] pamoja nawe; hukukosa kitu."'
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amebariki kazi zote za mikono yako. Amekutunza ulipokuwa ukipita katika nyika hii kubwa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekuwa pamoja nawe miaka hii arobaini, wala hujapungukiwa na kitu chochote."'
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amebariki kila kitu ulichofanya. Amekutunza katika safari yako ndefu kupitia jangwa hili kubwa mno. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekuwa pamoja nawe miaka yote hii arobaini, nawe umekuwa na kila kitu ulichohitaji."'

ko.L: 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 네 손이 하는 모든 일에 너에게 복을 주셨기 때문이다. 그분께서 네가 이 큰 광야를 걸어온 것을 아셨다. 이 사십 년 동안 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너와 함께 계셨으니, 너는 아무것도 부족하지 않았다."'
ko.B: 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 네가 손으로 한 모든 일에 복을 주셨다. 네가 이 넓은 광야를 지나는 동안 그분께서 너를 지켜보아 주셨다. 이 사십 년 동안 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너와 함께 계셨으므로, 너는 아무것도 모자란 것이 없었다."'
ko.R: 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희가 하는 모든 일에 복을 주셨다. 이 넓은 광야를 지나는 먼 길에서도 그분께서 너희를 돌보아 주셨다. 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 사십 년 동안 너희와 함께 계셨으므로, 너희는 필요한 것이 늘 있었다."'

decisions.choice: for: the reason Israel can pay its way
decisions.reason: The blessing God has given explains why Israel can buy food and water instead of taking them (verse 6): the people have the means to pay, and God has never let them go without.

decisions.choice: he has known your walking: he has watched over and cared for your journey
decisions.reason: To "know" here is to take notice of and care for, as in Psalm 1:6, "the LORD knows the way of the righteous".

decisions.choice: your, you: singular here, where verses 4-6 are plural
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy often moves between "you" plural and "you" singular. The singular speaks to Israel as one people; the meaning does not change.

decisions.choice: these forty years: the whole time since the exodus
decisions.reason: Forty years is the span of the wilderness journey (Numbers 14:33-34); verse 14 counts thirty-eight of them from Kadesh-barnea.

decisions.choice: has cared for you as you made your way / has watched over you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "has known your walking", which in English would sound like mere information.

decisions.choice: Balanced keeps the singular "너" for this verse, as the meaning decision notes that the Hebrew turns singular here
decisions.reason: The change from plural to singular is marked by the meaning decision, and the verse is wholly singular, so Balanced follows it; Readable, where God is speaking, keeps one plural "너희" for the whole message.

records.literal_gloss: And we passed on from with our brothers, [the] sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir, from [the] way of the Arabah, from Elath and from Ezion-geber; and we turned and passed on [by the] way of [the] wilderness of Moab.

en.L: And we passed on away from our brothers the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, away from the way of the Arabah, from Elath and from Ezion-geber. And we turned and passed on [by] the way of the wilderness of Moab.
en.B: So we moved on past our relatives, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, leaving the road through the Arabah that comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and went along the road through the wilderness of Moab.
en.R: So we kept going and left our relatives, Esau's descendants, behind in Seir. We left the road through the Arabah valley that comes up from the towns of Elath and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and took the road through the desert of Moab.

es.L: Y pasamos de largo, lejos de nuestros hermanos, los hijos de Esaú, que habitan en Seír, lejos del camino del Arabá, de Elat y de Ezión-geber; y nos volvimos y pasamos por el camino del desierto de Moab.
es.B: Así que seguimos adelante, dejando atrás a nuestros parientes, los descendientes de Esaú que viven en Seír, y apartándonos del camino del Arabá que sube desde Elat y Ezión-geber. Luego dimos la vuelta y tomamos el camino del desierto de Moab.
es.R: Así que seguimos nuestro camino y dejamos atrás a nuestros parientes, los descendientes de Esaú, en Seír. Dejamos el camino del valle del Arabá, que sube desde las ciudades de Elat y Ezión-geber. Después dimos la vuelta y tomamos el camino que atraviesa el desierto de Moab.

fr.L: Et nous sommes passés loin de nos frères, les fils d’Ésaü, qui habitent en Séir, loin du chemin de l’Araba, loin d’Élath et d’Etsion-Guéber ; puis nous nous sommes tournés et nous avons passé par le chemin du désert de Moab.
fr.B: Nous avons donc continué notre route en laissant de côté nos proches parents, les descendants d’Ésaü qui habitent en Séir, et en quittant la route de l’Araba qui monte d’Élath et d’Etsion-Guéber. Puis nous avons tourné et pris la route du désert de Moab.
fr.R: Nous avons donc continué notre chemin et laissé derrière nous nos proches, les descendants d’Ésaü, en Séir. Nous avons quitté la route de la vallée de l’Araba, qui monte depuis les villes d’Élath et d’Etsion-Guéber. Puis nous avons tourné et pris la route du désert de Moab.

sw.L: Basi tukapita mbali na ndugu zetu, wana wa Esau, wakaao Seiri, mbali na njia ya Araba, kutoka Elathi na kutoka Esion-geberi; kisha tukageuka, tukapita kwa njia ya nyika ya Moabu.
sw.B: Basi tukaendelea mbele, tukawapita ndugu zetu, wazao wa Esau wanaoishi Seiri, tukaiacha njia ya Araba inayopanda kutoka Elathi na Esion-geberi. Kisha tukageuka, tukashika njia ya nyika ya Moabu.
sw.R: Basi tuliendelea na safari, tukawaacha nyuma ndugu zetu, wazao wa Esau, huko Seiri. Tuliiacha njia ya bonde la Araba, inayopanda kutoka miji ya Elathi na Esion-geberi. Kisha tukageuka, tukashika njia inayopita katika jangwa la Moabu.

ko.L: 그리고 우리는 세일에 사는 우리 형제 에서의 자손을 떠나 지나갔고, 아라바 길, 곧 엘랏과 에시온게벨에서 [오는 길을] 떠났다. 그리고 우리는 방향을 돌려 모압 광야 길로 지나갔다.
ko.B: 그래서 우리는 세일에 사는 우리 친족 에서의 자손을 지나쳐 갔고, 엘랏과 에시온게벨에서 올라오는 아라바 길을 벗어났다. 그런 다음 우리는 방향을 돌려 모압 광야로 가는 길을 따라갔다.
ko.R: 그래서 우리는 계속 나아가서, 세일에 사는 우리 친척 에서의 자손을 뒤로하고 떠났습니다. 우리는 엘랏과 에시온게벨 성읍에서 올라오는 아라바 골짜기 길에서 벗어났습니다. 그러고는 방향을 돌려 모압 광야를 지나는 길로 갔습니다.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, Elath, Ezion-geber: the rift valley south of the Dead Sea and the towns at its southern end
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the dry valley that runs from the Dead Sea down to the gulf east of Sinai. Elath and Ezion-geber stood at the head of that gulf (1 Kings 9:26).

decisions.choice: away from ... away from the way of the Arabah: Israel left both Edom and the Arabah road behind
alternatives: passed by Edom by way of the Arabah road
decisions.reason: The same word "from" is repeated: Israel moved away from Edom's people and away from the road through the Arabah. The verse can also be read as saying that Israel went past Edom by way of that road. Either way, Israel then turned north-east toward Moab without taking any of Edom's land.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Moab: the open country on Moab's eastern edge
decisions.reason: Israel kept to the steppe east of Moab's farmland and towns, as Numbers 21:11 also says.

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: the Arabah valley, the towns of
decisions.reason: Readable adds "valley" and "the towns of" so that the reader knows what kind of places these names are.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶל־תָּ֨צַר֙אֶת־מוֹאָ֔ב וְאַל־תִּתְגָּ֥ר בָּ֖ם מִלְחָמָ֑ה כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֨ן לְךָ֤ מֵֽאַרְצוֹ֙ יְרֻשָּׁ֔ה כִּ֣י לִבְנֵי־ל֔וֹט נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־עָ֖ר יְרֻשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to me, Do not harass Moab, and do not engage in strife with them [in] battle, for not I will give to you of his land [as] a possession, for to [the] sons of Lot I have given Ar [as] a possession.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not harass Moab, and do not provoke them to battle, for I will not give you any of his land [as] a possession, for to the sons of Lot I have given Ar [as] a possession.'
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not treat Moab as an enemy or start a war with them. I will not give you any of their land to possess, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their own.'
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told me, 'Do not attack the Moabites or start a war with them. I will not give you any of their land. I have given Ar to Lot's descendants to be their own.'

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: “No hostigues a Moab, ni lo provoques a la guerra, porque no te daré de su tierra [como] posesión, porque a los hijos de Lot he dado Ar [como] posesión.”
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: “No trates a Moab como enemigo ni le hagas la guerra. No te daré nada de su tierra como posesión, porque Ar se la he dado a los descendientes de Lot para que sea suya.”
es.R: Luego {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: “No ataques a los moabitas ni empieces una guerra con ellos. No te daré nada de su tierra. Ar se la he dado a los descendientes de Lot para que sea de ellos.”

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : “Ne harcèle pas Moab et ne le provoque pas au combat, car je ne te donnerai rien de son pays [en] possession, car c’est aux fils de Loth que j’ai donné Ar [en] possession.”
fr.B: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : “Ne traite pas Moab en ennemi et ne lui déclare pas la guerre. Je ne te donnerai aucune partie de son territoire en possession, car j’ai donné Ar aux descendants de Loth pour qu’elle leur appartienne.”
fr.R: Ensuite, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : “N’attaque pas les Moabites et ne leur fais pas la guerre. Je ne te donnerai rien de leur pays. J’ai donné Ar aux descendants de Loth pour qu’elle soit à eux.”

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, 'Usimsumbue Moabu, wala usiwachokoze vitani, kwa maana sitakupa sehemu ya nchi yake [kuwa] milki, kwa sababu nimewapa wana wa Lutu Ari [kuwa] milki.'
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, 'Usimfanye Moabu kuwa adui wako wala usianzishe vita nao. Sitakupa sehemu yoyote ya nchi yao iwe milki yako, kwa sababu nimewapa wazao wa Lutu Ari iwe yao.'
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, 'Usiwashambulie Wamoabu wala usianzishe vita nao. Sitakupa sehemu yoyote ya nchi yao. Nimewapa wazao wa Lutu Ari iwe yao.'

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. '너는 모압을 괴롭히지 말고 그들과 전쟁을 일으키지 말라. 내가 그의 땅은 하나도 너에게 소유로 주지 않을 것이다. 내가 아르를 롯의 자손에게 소유로 주었기 때문이다.'
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. '모압을 원수처럼 대하지 말고 그들과 전쟁을 벌이지 말라. 나는 그들의 땅을 하나도 너희에게 소유로 주지 않을 것이다. 아르는 내가 롯의 자손에게 소유로 주었기 때문이다.'
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨습니다. '모압 사람들을 공격하거나 그들과 전쟁을 일으키지 말라. 나는 그들의 땅을 하나도 너희에게 주지 않겠다. 아르는 내가 롯의 자손에게 주어 그들의 땅이 되게 했다.'

decisions.choice: the sons of Lot: Moab and Ammon, descended from Abraham's nephew Lot
decisions.reason: Genesis 19:36-38 traces Moab and Ammon to Lot's two sons. Like Edom, they are relatives of Israel, and God protects their lands for that reason (verse 19).

decisions.choice: harass: treat as an enemy, press hard
decisions.reason: The verb means to be hostile to someone, to besiege or hem them in. Israel is not to act as Moab's enemy at all.

decisions.choice: Ar: a chief town of Moab, standing for Moab's land
decisions.reason: Ar lay near the Arnon, Moab's northern border (Numbers 21:15, 28). Here, as in verses 18 and 29, it stands for Moab's country as a whole.

decisions.choice: his land: Moab spoken of as one person
decisions.reason: Hebrew can speak of a nation as "he". "His land" is the land of Moab, and "them" earlier in the verse is its people.

decisions.choice: their land
decisions.reason: English does not usually call a nation "he"; Balanced and Readable say "their land", and Readable names the Moabites.

source.text: הָאֵמִ֥ים לְפָנִ֖ים יָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֑הּ עַ֣ם גָּד֥וֹל וְרַ֛ב וָרָ֖ם כָּעֲנָקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: The Emim formerly dwelt in it, a people great and numerous and tall like the Anakim.

en.L: (The Emim formerly lived in it, a people great and many and tall like the Anakim.
en.B: (In earlier times the Emim lived there, a great people, numerous and as tall as the Anakim.
en.R: (Long ago a people called the Emim lived in that land. They were a powerful nation with many people, and they were as tall as the Anakim.

es.L: (Los emitas habitaron antes en ella, un pueblo grande y numeroso y alto como los anaquitas.
es.B: (En tiempos antiguos vivían allí los emitas, un pueblo grande, numeroso y tan alto como los anaquitas.
es.R: (Hace mucho tiempo vivía en aquella tierra un pueblo llamado los emitas. Eran una nación poderosa, con mucha gente, y tan altos como los anaquitas.

fr.L: (Les Émim y habitaient autrefois, un peuple grand et nombreux et de haute taille comme les Anakim.
fr.B: (Autrefois, les Émim habitaient ce pays : un peuple grand, nombreux et de haute taille comme les Anakim.
fr.R: (Il y a longtemps, un peuple appelé les Émim vivait dans ce pays. C’était une nation puissante, avec beaucoup de gens, et ils étaient aussi grands que les Anakim.

sw.B: (Zamani Waemi waliishi huko, taifa kubwa, lenye watu wengi na warefu kama Waanaki.

decisions.choice: verses 10-12 are an explanatory aside about the peoples who held these lands before
decisions.reason: The LORD's words to Moses stop at the end of verse 9 and take up again in verse 13 ("Now get up and cross ..."). In between stands a note, in the style of a historian, about who lived in Moab and Seir before Moab and Edom. It shows that God had already given lands to Lot's and Esau's descendants by removing peoples as strong as the Anakim, whom Israel had been afraid of (1:28). It is still part of the book's account of Moses' speech, which continues.

decisions.choice: the Emim: the Moabites' name for the earlier people of their land
decisions.reason: Verse 11 says the name was the one the Moabites used. It may mean "the frightening ones"; the Emim are also named in Genesis 14:5. Nothing else is known of them.

decisions.choice: the Anakim: a people famous for their height
decisions.reason: The spies had seen the Anakim in Canaan and called them giants (Numbers 13:22, 28, 33), and fear of them was one reason Israel refused to enter the land (1:28).

decisions.choice: parentheses around verses 10-12
decisions.reason: Parentheses show the reader that these verses are a note set into the LORD's words, not words spoken to Moses. The names Emim and Anakim keep the Hebrew plural ending, as the source data spells them.

decisions.choice: "los emitas", "los anaquitas" (and "los refaítas", "los zamzumitas", verses 11 and 20)
alternatives: "los emim", "los anaquim", keeping the Hebrew plural as the English does
decisions.reason: Spanish names these peoples with its ordinary ending for peoples, as Genesis 14:5 already does ("los emitas", "los refaítas", "los zuzitas"), rather than with the Hebrew plural ending the English keeps.

decisions.choice: "Waemi", "Waanaki" (and "Warefai", "Wazamzumi", verses 11 and 20)
decisions.reason: Swahili names a people with the prefix wa-, as Genesis 14:5 does ("Waemi", "Warefai", "Wazuzi"), so the Hebrew plural ending is dropped.

decisions.choice: "엠 사람", "아낙 사람", "르바임", "삼숨밈", "호리 사람", "아위 사람", "갑돌 사람" for the earlier peoples of verses 10-23
decisions.reason: The forms follow Genesis 14 and Joshua in Korean (엠 사람, 호리 사람, 아위 사람, 르바임); 아낙 is used as a people's name here, where 1:28 speaks of the "아낙 자손". The Korean keeps the parentheses as the English does.

en.R: People thought of them as Rephaim, just like the Anakim. But the Moabites called them Emim.

decisions.choice: Rephaim: a general name for the tall ancient peoples of the region
decisions.reason: The Rephaim appear in Genesis 14:5 and 15:20, and Og king of Bashan was the last of them (3:11). Each people that took over their land had its own name for them: Emim in Moab, Zamzummim in Ammon (verse 20).

decisions.choice: call: the name in use among the Moabites
decisions.reason: The verb form describes what the Moabites customarily called them, and can be read as present ("call") or past ("used to call").

records.literal_gloss: And in Seir dwelt the Horites formerly, and [the] sons of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them and dwelt in their place, as did Israel to [the] land of his possession which gave Yahweh to them.

en.L: And in Seir the Horites formerly lived, but the sons of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them and lived in their place, as Israel did to the land of its possession, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to them.)
en.B: Seir, too, was once the home of the Horites. The descendants of Esau took it from them, wiping them out as they advanced and settling in their place, just as Israel did in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave it to possess.)
en.R: The Horites used to live in Seir. But Esau's descendants forced them out and wiped them out, and then they settled where the Horites had lived. This is just what Israel did in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them to be their own.)

es.L: Y en Seír habitaron antes los horeos, pero los hijos de Esaú los desposeyeron y los destruyeron delante de ellos, y habitaron en su lugar, como hizo Israel con la tierra de su posesión, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les dio.)
es.B: También Seír fue en otro tiempo la tierra de los horeos. Los descendientes de Esaú se la quitaron, exterminándolos a medida que avanzaban, y se establecieron en su lugar, como lo hizo Israel en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio en posesión.)
es.R: Los horeos vivían antes en Seír. Pero los descendientes de Esaú los echaron y acabaron con ellos, y después se quedaron a vivir donde los horeos habían vivido. Es lo mismo que hizo Israel en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les dio para que fuera suya.)

fr.L: Et en Séir habitaient autrefois les Horiens, mais les fils d’Ésaü les ont dépossédés et les ont détruits devant eux, et ils ont habité à leur place, comme Israël l’a fait pour le pays de sa possession, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur a donné.)
fr.B: Séir, de son côté, était autrefois le pays des Horiens. Les descendants d’Ésaü le leur ont pris, en les exterminant à mesure qu’ils avançaient, et se sont installés à leur place, comme Israël l’a fait dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a donné en possession.)
fr.R: Les Horiens vivaient autrefois en Séir. Mais les descendants d’Ésaü les ont chassés et les ont exterminés, puis ils se sont installés là où les Horiens avaient vécu. C’est exactement ce qu’Israël a fait dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné aux Israélites pour qu’il soit à eux.)

sw.B: Seiri nayo zamani ilikuwa nchi ya Wahori. Wazao wa Esau wakaichukua kutoka kwao, wakiwaangamiza walipokuwa wakisonga mbele, nao wakakaa mahali pao, kama vile Israeli alivyofanya katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa iwe milki yake.)

ko.L: 그리고 세일에는 전에 호리 사람이 살았는데, 에서의 자손이 그들을 쫓아내고 그들 앞에서 그들을 멸하고 그들의 자리에 살았다. 이스라엘이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 주신 자기 소유의 땅에 한 것과 같았다.)
ko.B: 세일에도 전에는 호리 사람들이 살았다. 에서의 자손이 쳐들어가면서 그들을 멸하여 쫓아내고 그 자리에 자리 잡았다. 이것은 이스라엘이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 소유로 주신 땅에서 한 것과 같았다.)
ko.R: 세일에는 전에 호리 사람들이 살았습니다. 그러나 에서의 자손이 그들을 쫓아내고 멸했습니다. 그리고 호리 사람들이 살던 곳에 자리 잡고 살았습니다. 이것은 이스라엘이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 주신 땅에서 한 것과 똑같았습니다.)

decisions.choice: the Horites: the earlier people of Seir
decisions.reason: Genesis 14:6 names the Horites in their hill country of Seir, and Genesis 36:20-30 lists their clans before Edom's.

decisions.choice: dispossessed: drove them out and took over their land
decisions.reason: The verb used here is the one used for Israel taking possession of its land, and for driving out the nations in it. It joins the two halves of the verse: Edom did to the Horites what Israel did in its own land.

decisions.choice: from before them: as they advanced
decisions.reason: "From before them" means in front of the descendants of Esau, as they moved in.

decisions.choice: as Israel did: the note looks back from a later time
alternatives: the land east of the Jordan, taken in 2:31-3:17
the whole land, after the conquest
decisions.reason: The aside speaks of Israel's taking of its land as already done. It may have in view the land east of the Jordan, which Israel took in this chapter and the next (2:31-3:17) and which was given to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (3:12-20); or it may look back on the whole land, written from a time after Israel had settled there.

decisions.choice: which the LORD gave to them: the land is God's gift
decisions.reason: Even in a note about other peoples, Israel's land is the land the LORD gave, as Seir was given to Esau (verse 5).

decisions.choice: took it from them / forced them out
decisions.reason: "Dispossess" is the Literal word; Balanced and Readable say what it means for a people. Balanced also speaks of Israel as "it", a nation, where the Hebrew has "its possession" and "to them".

decisions.choice: The asides of verses 10-12 and 20-23 are in 합쇼체 at Readable, as part of Moses' address
alternatives: plain written style as a narrator's note
decisions.reason: The English sets these notes inside Moses' speech, in parentheses; Readable keeps the speech level of the address around them so the text does not seem to change speaker.

records.literal_gloss: Now arise and pass over the wadi of Zered. And we passed over the wadi of Zered.

en.L: 'Now arise and cross over the wadi of Zered.' And we crossed over the wadi of Zered.
en.B: 'Rise now and cross over the Zered Valley.' So we crossed over the Zered Valley.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, 'Now get going and cross the Zered Valley.' So we crossed it.

es.L: “Ahora {{plural_you:levántense|levantaos}} y {{plural_you:crucen|cruzad}} el torrente de Zered.” Y cruzamos el torrente de Zered.
es.B: “{{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}} ahora y {{plural_you:crucen|cruzad}} el valle de Zered.” Así que cruzamos el valle de Zered.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: “Ahora {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} en marcha y {{plural_you:crucen|cruzad}} el valle de Zered.” Y lo cruzamos.

fr.L: “Maintenant, levez-vous et passez le torrent du Zéred.” Et nous avons passé le torrent du Zéred.
fr.B: “Levez-vous maintenant et traversez la vallée du Zéred.” Nous avons donc traversé la vallée du Zéred.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : “Maintenant, en route ! Traversez la vallée du Zéred.” Alors nous l’avons traversée.

sw.L: 'Sasa ondokeni mvuke kijito cha Zeredi.' Nasi tukavuka kijito cha Zeredi.
sw.B: 'Ondokeni sasa mvuke Bonde la Zeredi.' Basi tukavuka Bonde la Zeredi.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema, 'Sasa ondokeni, mvuke Bonde la Zeredi.' Basi tukalivuka.

ko.L: '이제 일어나 세렛 골짜기를 건너라.' 그래서 우리는 세렛 골짜기를 건넜다.
ko.B: '이제 일어나 세렛 골짜기를 건너가라.' 그래서 우리는 세렛 골짜기를 건넜다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨습니다. '이제 일어나 세렛 골짜기를 건너가거라.' 그래서 우리는 그 골짜기를 건넜습니다.

decisions.choice: the LORD's words from verse 9 take up again here
decisions.reason: After the aside of verses 10-12, the command goes on from where verse 9 stopped. The speaker is the LORD.

decisions.choice: the wadi of Zered: the stream valley on Moab's southern border
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley that carries water in the rainy season and is often dry the rest of the year. The Zered lay between Edom and Moab (Numbers 21:12). Crossing it marked the end of the wilderness years (verse 14).

decisions.choice: The LORD said
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, since the aside has come between the start of the LORD's words and this command.

decisions.choice: the Zered Valley
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:12: Literal says "wadi"; Balanced and Readable use a common English word.

decisions.choice: "le torrent du Zéred" (L), "la vallée du Zéred" (B, R); likewise "le torrent de l'Arnon" (verse 24)
decisions.reason: "Torrent" is the usual French word for a stream that runs only after the rains, which is what a wadi is; "oued" is the Arabic loanword, known in North Africa but not everywhere. Balanced and Readable follow the English "valley".

decisions.choice: "kijito cha Zeredi" (L), "Bonde la Zeredi" (B, R); likewise "kijito cha Arnoni" (verse 24)
decisions.reason: Literal names the seasonal stream itself, "kijito"; Balanced and Readable follow the English "valley" with "bonde".

decisions.choice: "골짜기" for the wadi at every level (세렛 골짜기, 아르논 골짜기, 얍복 골짜기); Readable says "아르논 강" and "얍복강" where the English Readable says river
decisions.reason: A wadi is a stream valley that runs with water only in the wet season; "골짜기" is the Korean word Joshua uses for the Arnon.
